correctness.rationale: The 27 closed radius-one balls are generated from Hamming coordinates. Exhaustive reconstruction gives f=(27,243,891,945,567,189,27) and 2,889 nonempty simplices. The checker builds 11,097 Hasse covers, an acyclic 1,377-pair matching, and verifies exactly one critical 0-cell and 134 critical 2-cells by a global DAG topological sort. The resulting Morse CW complex is a wedge of 134 two-spheres, proving integral homology, not just finite-field ranks.

evidence: Adams–Shukla–Singh explicitly restrict the main scale-two classification to binary hypercube graphs.
Matsushita Example 3.5 explicitly computes closed-neighborhood complexes of two-factor products K_m Cartesian K_n; this H(3,3) has three factors.
Matsushita Theorem 1.2 gives suspension of the closed-neighborhood complex as an independence complex of a canonical double cover, but not the latter homotopy type for this ternary threefold graph.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The binary-cube theorem does not apply to alphabet size three. The two-factor product formula does not directly give three-factor product topology, since closed-neighborhood complexes do not generally preserve Cartesian graph products. The general reduction does not itself evaluate the relevant independence complex.

value.rationale: The ternary 3-dimensional Hamming cube is the first genuinely nonbinary threefold Cartesian product of complete graphs. Its complete 134-sphere homotopy determination extends two disjoint known axes (binary cubes and two-factor rook graphs) and supplies a reproducible natural benchmark, without asserting an unsupported uniform extension.
